items.title: Qualify Codex protocol to schema to Python SDK projection
items.summary: Codex now exposes a concrete Python SDK whose generated Pydantic models are produced from a runtime-emitted aggregate v2 schema bundle. ctrl should qualify the projection chain instead of treating CLI behavior as an opaque surface.
items.localContractImpact: Add Codex schema/SDK projection qualification to ctrl's OpenAI integration and future Python-native controller adapter.

observations.observation: Current main exports a draft-07 ClientRequest JSON schema; blob f9907887a4a3ea6d75e54d3c93448b1ee5609255.
The openai-codex Python SDK is present and pins openai-codex-cli-bin==0.144.4; blob a6ff55ee7480d98a1b4dd15d33a9aa5372285d33.

SDK artifact generation reads the exact runtime package pin and names codex_app_server_protocol.v2.schemas.json as the aggregate schema bundle emitted by the runtime binary; blob 33dfae57c2fa932e217e49d27551fc534d7cbe16.

claims.text: The Python SDK is a first-class generated projection of runtime-emitted Codex app-server schemas and should be qualified as a projection edge.

items.title: Treat rollout bundles and reduced graphs as correlated runtime evidence
items.summary: Codex rollout tracing explicitly records ordered raw runtime evidence and deterministically reduces it into a semantic graph. ctrl can use the pair as a replay/correlation surface but must preserve raw-versus-reduced identity.
items.localContractImpact: Define rollout bundle identity, raw payload references, reduction/reconstruction correlation, lineage, and sensitive-evidence handling in ctrl.

observations.observation: Rollout Trace documents local raw bundles, ordered trace.jsonl and payloads, and a deterministic replay_bundle reducer that produces a semantic graph while preserving raw payload references; blob 540a494638d8fe4f2968c49cef50cb81283d6381.

claims.text: ctrl should model live runtime observations and reconstructed rollout observations as related but non-identical evidence planes.

items.title: Establish hook/tool interception as a future blocking boundary
items.summary: The current Codex hook model exposes session, turn, permission, tool, tool-use, transcript, mutation, blocking, and additional-context fields that directly intersect ctrl's configured PreToolUse/PostToolUse controller boundary.
items.localContractImpact: Baseline only. Future incompatible changes to these hook identities or semantics should classify at blocking-gate for ctrl.

observations.observation: PreToolUseRequest includes session_id, turn_id, cwd, transcript_path, model, permission_mode, tool_name, tool_use_id and tool_input; outcome includes should_block, block_reason, additional contexts and updated input; blob 7233c014a96980a8b207b9d8cb7a1440197ef2fd.

claims.text: Current hook semantics are sufficiently explicit to establish an exact ctrl baseline for future blocking-gate comparison.

items.title: Use CPython's compiler pipeline as an executable dependency DAG
items.summary: CPython 3.14's compiler source explicitly documents the AST-to-symbol-table-to-instruction-sequence-to-CFG-to-code-object pipeline. This is strong upstream evidence for a typed dependency DAG driving impact closure, regrtest selection, and local probes.
items.localContractImpact: Implement the declared CPython DAG in ctrl and bind changed paths to reverse dependency closure plus selected test/probe operations.

observations.observation: Python/compile.c states that _PyAST_Compile returns a PyCodeObject and enumerates passes for future checks, symbol table, instruction sequence/codegen, control-flow graph optimization, and final assembly; blob 6c5ef5329ffc3aaef424f47f7f67a99eddfbede0.

claims.text: The CPython compiler dependency graph can be grounded in upstream implementation structure rather than maintained as an unqualified local taxonomy.

items.title: Operationalize CPython regrtest behind a process adapter
items.summary: CPython 3.14 exposes regrtest as the regression-suite runner and keeps detailed runner/result machinery under test.libregrtest. ctrl should select regrtest slices from the DAG but invoke them through the checked-out interpreter process, keeping internal runner modules observational rather than dependency APIs.
items.localContractImpact: Implement ResolveRevision/ResolveBuild/SelectRegrtests/RunRegrtests plus normalized process-result observations, alongside a separate local-probe execution path.

observations.observation: Lib/test/regrtest.py identifies itself as the Python regression test runner and delegates to test.libregrtest.main; blob 46a74fe276f55307b3e368b073661547e46de1c7.

libregrtest contains specialized regression result and capture logic, confirming that ctrl should observe its outputs without treating these internal modules as a stable library boundary; blob 1820f354572521accb4ec7340942f8b13505d0e2.

claims.text: The qualified ctrl adapter should invoke selected CPython regression tests through ./python -m test and normalize process evidence, while local probes remain a separate evidence family.

items.title: Bind sys.monitoring probes to interpreter instrumentation and frame/code state
items.summary: CPython 3.14 instrumentation directly maps opcodes to monitoring events and depends on code, frame, interpreter-frame, optimizer, and free-threaded runtime machinery. A ctrl monitoring probe should therefore preserve code/instruction/frame correlation and record runtime mode.
items.localContractImpact: Implement normalized monitoring-event and frame-source probes with explicit runtime/build identity, including free-threaded mode as a distinct observation dimension.

observations.observation: Python/instrumentation.c maps instruction opcodes to monitoring events, uses code/frame/interpreter-frame internals, and contains separate free-threaded synchronization paths; blob 0a7400c26993b32bf538fc15f892f63d1e02149f.

claims.text: A useful monitoring witness must correlate monitoring events with code objects, instructions, frames, and runtime mode rather than emit an untyped callback log.
